chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajali narrated to me. He said: Hammad ibn Waqid narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) that he said:
Whoever says "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, glory be to Allah the Great" thirty times will receive riches, leave poverty behind, and knock on the gate of Paradise.

key_terms.الغنى: Wealth, richness - here referring to both material and spiritual sufficiency
key_terms.الفقر: Poverty, want - the opposite condition that is dispelled through dhikr
key_terms.باب الجنة: Gate of Paradise - metaphor for attaining closeness to Paradise
key_terms.سبحان الله: Subhanallah - Glory be to Allah, a phrase of divine glorification (tasbih)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of saying Subhanallah wa bihamdihi thirty times?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that reciting the tasbih phrase "Subhanallah wa bihamdihi, Subhanallah al-'Azim" thirty times brings three benefits: wealth, freedom from poverty, and a path toward Paradise. This hadith was narrated in the scholarly circle of Shaykh al-Saduq in 368 AH during a Friday assembly, emphasizing the material and spiritual rewards of this specific form of dhikr, a formula also mentioned in Prophetic traditions as being beloved to Allah and heavy on the scales of deeds.
